messages:
olivia: Quick follow-up on pinning metadata evolution. I went back to the rollout metadata RFC and want to propose we avoid mutating the existing 'pin' object shape and instead introduce new top-level keys to express intent. Specifically: a) rollout_schema_v: integer b) pin_source: enum('user','auto','system') c) compat: {fallback_order: [...], strict: boolean}

sam: Can you sketch an example? I'm mostly worried about old clients failing when they receive unknown keys.

olivia: Example payload below — server would include rollout_schema_v so clients can branch. Old clients ignore unknown top-level keys.

```
{
  "rollout_schema_v": 2,
  "pin": {
    "model": "redwood-ev1",
    "version": "2026-03-01"
  },
  "pin_source": "auto",
  "compat": {
    "fallback_order": ["redwood-ev1-quant","redwood-ev1-32bit"],
    "strict": false
  }
}
```

ravi: Runtime note: if we start returning compat.fallback_order the routing layer needs to treat that as advisory only. We shouldn't change cache key semantics until we have client opt-in. Otherwise we'll explode cache fragmentation.

maria: +1 to not changing cache keys. Ops ask: how long do we run dual outputs (old + new) so SDKs have time to upgrade?

olivia: Proposal: dual-write for 8 weeks (emit both the legacy 'pin' and the new keys), measure client usage via telemetry (client-sdk headers), then remove legacy iff <1% legacy usage and no errors.

ada: For clients that don't parse JSON strictly (we have some tiny Go services), adding unknown top-level keys is safe. But if we rename fields inside 'pin' that's risky. So landing new top-level keys is the least disruptive.

sam: Should we add a 'rollout_schema_v' to the HTTP response headers too? Faster client branching for proxies.

ravi: +1 header. Also add a server-side validator that rejects any rollout payload that mixes incompatible fields (e.g., pin.version as int vs string). That will avoid accidental shapes.

maria: SDK owners: we should add a deprecation warning to the SDK logs when legacy-only pin descriptors are returned. That gives app owners visibility.

deploy-bot: Canary deploy started: rollout-metadata-v2 canary (10% traffic) at 2026-03-20T14:12Z :rocket:

olivia: For migration steps: 1) update control plane to emit rollout_schema_v + compat 2) add header rollout-schema-v 3) dual-write payloads 4) bump SDKs and ship validators with warning logs 5) monitor for 8 weeks 6) schedule hard cut if metrics OK.

ada: One more ask: add a small 'unknown_fields' telemetry metric per tenant so we can identify clients choking on changes.

ravi: Agree. Also add a runtime toggle to force legacy-only payloads for specific tenants to debug.

sam: I'll own the SDK changes and release a patch with validator + warning. ETA 2 weeks.

maria: I'll own the rollout metrics/dashboard. Will add a panel for legacy-pin usage, unknown_fields by tenant, and fallback_invocation_count.

olivia: Thanks — actionables: sam (SDK patch), maria (dashboards), ravi (runtime toggle + cache guidance), ada (telemetry metric), ops (canary watch). I'll draft a short RFC follow-up and post here for sign-off by EOW.

sam: Sounds good. :thumbsup:

ravi: Small nit — recommend 90-day hard-deprecate window instead of 8 weeks if legal or enterprise customers need more runway. Can we add a tenant-level opt-in extension?

olivia: Good call. We'll keep server-level default 8 weeks but allow tenant-level extension up to 90 days via feature flag. I'll add to the doc.

maria: Noted. I'll reflect that in the dashboard (extension flags column).

olivia: Great. If no objections I'll publish the RFC patch tomorrow morning.
